question: Plutonic rocks are formed when lava cools ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**in the crust**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Plutonic rocks**, also known as intrusive igneous rocks, are formed when magma cools and solidifies **below the Earth's surface**, specifically in the crust.
 
• The slow cooling of magma allows the formation of large, visible **mineral crystals** in plutonic rocks.
 
• Common examples of plutonic rocks include **granite, diorite, and gabbro**, which are extensively used in construction and decorative purposes.
 
• Plutonic rocks are exposed to the surface over time due to **erosion and tectonic uplift**.
 
• The term "plutonic" is derived from Pluto, the Roman god of the underworld, symbolizing their formation deep within the Earth's crust.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Igneous rocks** are classified into two main types based on their formation: **intrusive (plutonic)** and **extrusive (volcanic)**.
 
• Intrusive rocks form **beneath the Earth's surface**, while extrusive rocks form **on the surface** when lava cools quickly.
 
• The cooling rate of magma determines the texture of igneous rocks—**slow cooling forms coarse-grained rocks**, while rapid cooling forms fine-grained rocks.
 
• Plutonic rocks are often associated with **large geological features** such as batholiths, laccoliths, and dikes.
 
• Understanding plutonic rocks helps geologists study the Earth's **interior processes, tectonics, and mineral resources**.
